content.title: About
content.content: A flavored decaffeinated iced latte is a cold coffee beverage made from roasted decaf coffee beans, milk, and natural flavorings. It retains the creamy latte profile without the stimulating effect of caffeine, making it suitable for evening consumption.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Decaffeinated coffee is produced either by extracting caffeine from regular beans or by using naturally low‑caffeine varieties.
Iced latte first gained popularity in the United States in the 1990s as a response to the growing demand for cold coffee drinks.
Natural flavorings (vanilla, caramel, nut) are often added after extraction to preserve their aromatic qualities.
Decaf drinks may contain up to 5 mg of caffeine per serving, far less than a regular latte (about 70 mg).
Cold brewing helps retain aroma because lower temperatures do not degrade volatile compounds.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Even without caffeine, decaf coffee retains polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports hydration
items.content: A cold, water‑rich beverage contributes to the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Lower acidity
items.content: The decaffeination process often reduces acidity, making the drink gentler on the stomach.

items.title: Enriched with milk
items.content: Milk adds calcium, vitamin D, and protein, supporting bone health.

items.title: Suitable for caffeine‑sensitive individuals
items.content: Ideal for people avoiding stimulants while still enjoying coffee flavor.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Those with lactose intolerance or milk allergy should opt for plant‑based alternatives.

items.title: Added sugar in flavorings
items.content: Some flavored syrups contain added sugars; check the label if you watch sugar intake.

items.title: Residual caffeine
items.content: Although low, the small amount of caffeine may still affect highly sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caloric content
items.content: Cream or sweet syrups increase the drink’s calories.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the decaf iced latte well‑chilled over ice, optionally adding natural syrup or spices such as cinnamon or nutmeg. Plant‑based milks—almond, oat, soy—can be used as alternatives.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared beverage in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours. If using a decaf coffee concentrate, keep it in a sealed container in a cool place and follow the manufacturer’s shelf‑life recommendations.
